But its closing sentence, "This also covers n=1, when C=0", is wrong about its own branch: at n=1 the module M is simple, so its only maximal proper submodule is 0 and A=B necessarily, making the A != B branch vacuous rather than covered. Taking the sentence at face value would put step 4.1's length count at n-2 = -1. The case is genuinely handled, by step 2.1's A = B branch.

prevention.ref: A reader that rewrites a proof owns its boundary sentences too; the rewrite was checked for validity but its inherited closing clause was not re-derived against the new argument.

subject: finite-smoke registers zero obligations across all 175 proof-bearing items in batches 1-3
subclass_note: finite-smoke.mjs reports "0 error(s), 0 check(s) over 0/26, 0/90, 0/59 item(s) carrying obligations" — it runs, exits zero and checks nothing, in three batches whose content is unusually rich in bounded finite claims: Sylow counts for groups of order at most fifteen, S_4, A_5 and Aff(Z/5); the length of Z/p^k; the reciprocity table for small odd primes; square-root counts modulo n; the order of Aut((Z/p)^2). These are exactly the claims a bounded countermodel search can falsify. The gate is green because nobody registered an obligation, which is indistinguishable in the output from a gate that searched and found nothing. CLOSED by Alpha contract-audit-3 (2026-08-17): the gate is live at 4 checks over 324 scoped items, and gate-liveness now reports "live finite-smoke 4 checks" instead of VACUOUS. Selected, each after reading the item and picking the registry check that probes ITS claim: binomial-congruence-solution-count on thm-unit-square-criterion-modulo-odd-prime-powers (exactly two solution classes; the search computes gcd(phi(p^k),2)=2 against actual counts), on lem-nonsingular-square-root-lift-modulo-odd-prime-powers (non-unique lifting would push the count above two at p^(k+1)), and on thm-unit-square-criterion-modulo-two-powers (reaches the modulus-2 and modulus-4 clauses only; 2^k for k>=3 has no primitive root and is outside the search by construction); cyclic-subgroup-lagrange on ex-length-of-z-modulo-p-to-the-k (the chain terms are the subgroups generated by p^i, whose orders the check computes). Three of this row's named candidates were declined on evidence rather than covered: the Sylow data table for orders at most fifteen (no registry check computes n_p = 1 mod p or n_p | m), the reciprocity table (no check computes Legendre symbols), and the order of Aut((Z/p)^2) (its step 4.1 states the argument "makes no matrix-group identification", so matrix-ring-laws-mod-n would test a route the proof deliberately avoids). Batch 3 and batches 4-7 carry no check: field theory, measure theory, topology and complex analysis match no registry entry, and the two poset checks are existence-of-failure witnesses for meets, whereas batch 7 asserts limit creation positively and its one failure item is a coequalizer in Set versus Grp. Detail and evidence: research/frontier-15-alpha-contract-audit.md.

prevention.ref: The tool-change half this row asked for already exists and is what caught the vacuity: gate-liveness.mjs distinguishes "searched, found nothing" from "no obligation registered" and reports VACUOUS with a nonzero exit, and the autopilot routes that vacuity to a contract-audit Alpha for check SELECTION (commit 1a63bc0b). What remained was the selection itself, which is judgement and is now done. finite-smoke.mjs also prints the coverage ratio (4/324) so the count can no longer be read as coverage.

subject: 17 proof steps across the level name a check and perform none, and 4 contract boundary rows credit such a step as `checked`
subclass_note: The class is a numbered step whose entire content is an imperative naming work: "We treat the trivial $p$-subgroup and primes not dividing $|G|$." (thm-sylow-second-theorem 4.1), "We check the trivial quotient." (thm-fitting-subgroup-of-the-frattini-quotient 3.1), "We treat repeated terms and the zero module." (thm-equivalent-characterizations-of-artinian-modules 3.1), "Keep the two prime orderings and the order-twelve boundary case explicit." (thm-groups-of-order-p-squared-q-have-a-normal-sylow-subgroup 4.1), "The preceding argument gives the conclusion under every hypothesis of the Statement." (4 items, contentless filler), "We check fields of characteristic two.", "We check the initial term $\mathbb Z$.", "We check the inverse map and the zero ring.", "Remove zero or repeated summands and include the zero-generated case.", "We apply orbit-stabiliser, including the unique/trivial Sylow case.", "The forward implication is published." (a repository status claim standing in for a step). Two items — prop-endomorphisms-form-a-ring and thm-endomorphism-ring-of-a-finite-direct-sum-as-hom-matrices — had NO proof at all: every numbered step was an announcement, one of them naming four ring axioms it never verified. Why this is a boundary defect and not only a prose defect: thm-sylow-second-theorem's contract marked `zero` and `degenerate` as `checked` with the evidence "is resolved in step 4.1", quoting the announcement verbatim. boundary-audit could not see it, because its `checked` detector only tests whether the credited step NUMBER exists in the proof, and 4.1 does exist. All 17 repaired: the real discharge written for each named case, and full proofs authored for the two items that had none. Each repaired item re-precheck'd, its contract entry regenerated, and proof-contract --strict re-run to 0 errors.

prevention.ref: Two tool changes, both live. (1) tools/announcement-steps.mjs, new: flags a numbered step whose every sentence opens by naming an activity and none of which states an outcome, splitting hits into `strong` and `weak` so a terse but real discharge is not swept up. Its verb list is grown from live misses, never guessed — the first version missed 2 of 3 known instances because inline math inside a NAMED case counted as work, and a later one missed "Keep the two prime orderings..." because `Keep` was absent. Cross-check it with an orthogonal scan (steps with no math, no relation symbol, under 170 chars) before trusting a zero result; that scan is noisy but it is what surfaced 3 further verbs. (2) tools/boundary-audit.mjs gains a fourth contradiction signal: a `checked` row crediting a step that IS an announcement, which is airtight because both halves are mechanical. Verified against a purpose-built fixture — it fires on the announcement-credited row and stays silent on the row crediting real work. NOT done, and deliberately: stripping the item's own title from the template-cluster key collapses frontier-15's interpolated rows into 31 clusters, but most are honest ('this item states no biconditional' is the true disposition for 45 items and has one natural phrasing), so it would make a precision-first gate noisy.

subject: thm-sylow-third-theorem chooses a Sylow subgroup with no dependency establishing that one exists, and declares a fact no step uses
subclass_note: Found by the independent DeepSeek refuter and confirmed from disk. Step 1.1 read "Let a Sylow subgroup $P$ act by conjugation on the Sylow set", which presupposes Syl_p(G) is nonempty — that is Sylow I, and thm-sylow-first-theorem appeared nowhere in `deps`. The item's own [L4] even says existence "is proved later". None of the five declared dependencies supplies it. Separately lem-product-with-normal-subgroup was declared as [L5] and used by no step. Both were invisible to proof-contract because step 1.1 carried a BLANKET citation of all five facts, which satisfies the every-fact-is-used check while telling the input map nothing true. Repaired: thm-sylow-first-theorem added to deps and to the facts block, step 1.1 rewritten to draw P from a set a cited fact has made nonempty, the unused fact removed, and steps 2.1 and 3.1 — which cited nothing at all while using Sylow II, the fixed-point congruence and the normalizer-index formula — written out with honest citations. The mathematics was correct throughout; only the dependency trace was false.

prevention.ref: The enabling pattern is the blanket citation: a first step listing every fact in the item, which makes `citation-uses` and `step-entry-input-omitted` vacuously satisfied for facts no step actually uses. Seen on at least 8 batch-2 items (thm-groups-of-order-one-hundred-five-... cites 12 at step 1.1, cor-classification-of-groups-of-order-one-hundred-five cites 15, ex-heisenberg-... cites 12). A proof-contract check worth writing: flag a step whose input list names more than N facts AND is the only step naming most of them; the honest cases are rare and can be upheld on the record like a boundary row.

subject: thm-sylow-second-theorem's title stated Sylow II with no finiteness marker
subclass_note: Reported as FATAL by the independent DeepSeek refuter, which supplied a correct counterexample: in the infinite dihedral group the maximal 2-subgroups <r^n s> split into two conjugacy classes by the parity of n, since conjugation sends r^n s to r^(n+2k) s or r^(2j-n) s. I verified that computation and it is right for the general notion of Sylow subgroup. I adjudicate it NONFATAL rather than fatal, on two pieces of evidence the refuter did not have: this library's def-sylow-p-subgroup is stated only for finite G, so the title's phrase cannot be read outside finite groups in-library; and a self-tested scan of the level found six other titles using the same convention (cor-sylow-subgroup-normal-iff-unique, thm-normalizer-of-a-sylow-normalizer, thm-frattini-argument, cor-frattini-subgroup-is-contained-in-the-fitting-subgroup, ex-a-four-is-not-nilpotent, cor-length-is-additive-in-short-exact-sequences). It was underspecified, not false in the library's own vocabulary. Title still amended to "in a finite group" as step-6 polish, because Sylow I and Sylow III both carry the marker and the title should stand alone in the index and flowchart, where the reader has not opened the definition.

prevention.ref: The scan that produced the six-item convention finding was itself broken on first run and returned zero hits — its `titleFinite` regex matched the very title it was meant to flag, so the empty result was meaningless. It only became evidence after a self-test asserting that the known-bad title flags and the repaired one clears. Any title/statement hypothesis-drift scan should carry that self-test inline; a zero-hit scan with no positive control is not a finding.

subject: risk-report reported 125 items unreviewed while 33 of them carried complete Alpha reviews under the wrong key
subclass_note: risk-report --require-reviewed demands risk_review.notes; Alpha-a had written its dispositions under risk_review.disposition. The 33 rows were substantive, per-item and in several cases recorded confirmed-fatal repairs with their own ledger rows — they were not missing work, they were a field-name mismatch, and the gate could not tell the two apart. I read all 33 before touching them and renamed the key; no rationale was written, weakened or invented to clear the gate. The remaining 92 were genuinely unreviewed and were read and reviewed individually. Recorded because the failure mode is worth naming: a gate that reports 'missing' cannot distinguish absent work from misfiled work, and the honest response to a large missing-count is to read the artifacts before assuming the work was never done.

prevention.ref: risk-report could distinguish the two cases cheaply: if contracts[id].risk_review exists but lacks `notes`, emit a distinct code (risk-review-malformed) naming the keys it did find, instead of the same risk-review-missing it emits for an absent block. The remedy line for the two is different — one is 'do the review', the other is 'rename the key' — and conflating them cost a full re-read of 33 completed reviews.

subject: 518 boundary rows across 88 batch-2 items are generated from the item's title and statement rather than written as dispositions
subclass_note: 26 items have a worksheet that is generated end to end and 62 are partly generated; batches 1 and 3-7 have none, so this is one Beta's habit and not a level-wide convention. The shape is "<title>: <stock clause for this axis> for \u201c<statement>\u201d", with `not_applicable` reasons drawn from a fixed set of seven phrasings ('has no set, family, sum, product, or series allowed to be empty', 'is a one-way assertion rather than a biconditional', ...) and `checked` evidence reading 'is resolved in step X.Y: "<verbatim step text>"'. boundary-audit's template detector reports NO cluster over these 518 rows, because interpolating each item's own title and statement makes every row textually unique — the normalizer strips the id and quoted spans but not the title. The independent DeepSeek refuter hit the same class from the other side on fs-finite-nilpotent-and-solvable-groups-coincide, whose iff-forward and iff-reverse rows call the claim 'a one-way assertion rather than a biconditional' when 'finite nilpotent and finite solvable groups are the same' is plainly an equivalence; I confirmed that from disk. NOT repaired at scale: rewriting 518 rows as real dispositions is the owning Beta's work with its sources to hand, and a bulk rewrite by me would reproduce the original defect in a new hand. The four rows that credited an announcement step ARE repaired, via f15-a-rr-001.

prevention.ref: The measurement is a 30-line script: count rows whose reason matches one of the seven stock tails or the 'is resolved in step X.Y:' frame, then group by item. Items at 8/8 are the ones to route back. Making boundary-audit itself fail on this needs care — stripping the title from the cluster key does collapse the rows, but it also collapses 45 honest 'this item states no biconditional' rows, and this tool's stated design is precision over recall because a detector firing on a third of the corpus trains readers to skim it.
